Subject: Equity issuance schedule: pre-board pricing window & 409A timing

Team —

We need to lock in dates for option issuances tied to the next board pricing window. Draft schedule attached (Equity_Schedule_v1.xlsx) plus a short scope for the 409A vendor (409A_scope.docx). Key asks:

- Can Finance confirm a cap-table cutoff / record date we should use for grant calculations?
- Legal: any outstanding sign-off required to permit issuance on the target dates?
- People Ops: which offers are contingent on this issuance timing (I flagged 3 ext offers: Priya N., one Director IC, one senior IC).

Target timeline I put in the sheet:
- Board packet & pricing docs due to board ops: Aug 28
- 409A vendor kickoff: Aug 24
- Grant execution window (employee-facing): Sep 2–4

If the 409A comes back delayed, we need a fallback (possible smaller grant now, remainder in the next window). Please reply with conflicts or firm dates by EOD Thu so I can lock a board packet.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Talent Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Equity_Schedule_v1.xlsx, 409A_scope.docx

Thanks, Hannah — I reviewed the draft schedule. A few practical notes:

- For pending offers: Priya N. (PE org) has an acceptance window to Sep 6; if we push issuance to Sep 2–4 we should be fine, but we must include language that grants are subject to board approval & effective date.
- For the Director-level role, hiring manager wants a start date of Sep 15; recommend we issue options with an effective date of Sep 2 but set the vesting commencement date aligned to start (detail in offer).
- Headcount approvals: the People Ops headcount worksheet is updated — there is a small risk if any of the three roles push beyond Sep 10, we may need to split grants across windows.

Also: signal to candidates that there might be a technical hold if 409A extends beyond Sep 1. I can draft the short candidate note (1–2 lines).

Laura

Quick finance perspective: we need to set an official cap-table cutoff. For prior windows we used the Friday before the board packet is finalized; proposing Aug 27 (EOD PT). That will allow us to reconcile grants and calculate strike prices against the cap on Aug 28.

About the 409A: I reached out to Wilson (cc'd) asking for an ETA — if they can turn on Aug 24 as planned, we can keep the Sep 2 issuance. If there is a >3 business day slip, we should not hold offers hostage; instead we should execute grants with provisional strike prices and run a batch true-up once 409A is complete. Legal: please confirm whether provisional grants plus subsequent true-up is reasonable from a compliance standpoint.

Also: any material blackouts (SEC/contractual) we must be aware of before issuing to external hires?

—Markus
